findings.quote: **Check 1.** A company enables the new AWS Security Hub. Will it show card numbers that Macie finds? ... No. Amazon Macie [is not automatically enabled](../facts/security-hub.md#security-hub-enables-cspm-not-macie).
findings.evidence: Fact security-hub-enables-cspm-not-macie only says that enabling Security Hub does not turn Macie on: "Amazon Macie for sensitive data discovery is not automatically enabled." The stem says "card numbers that Macie finds", so Macie is already running. The flat "No" therefore teaches that the new Security Hub never shows Macie findings. That contradicts 2-services.md (Security Hub card: "correlates signals from Security Hub CSPM, Amazon Inspector, Amazon Macie and Amazon GuardDuty"). Fix: ask "Does enabling the new Security Hub turn on Macie?" (answer: no, enable Macie yourself), or answer "Only after you enable Macie as well".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Same fix as claims-01.

findings.quote: **Check 2.** A proactive Config rule checks a template before deployment and finds it noncompliant. Is the deployment blocked?
findings.evidence: No section of the chapter teaches proactive rules. 2-deep.md lists only two trigger types ("Configuration change", "Periodic"), and its heading says Config judges a change "after the change is recorded". A proactive rule, which runs before deployment, goes against that gist and first appears inside a Check. Rule: READER.md ("questions must test what the gist misses", not what the chapter never taught). Fix: add one sentence or a Go deeper block in the Config subsection on the two evaluation modes, using fact config-guide-proactive-vs-detective ("There are two evaluation modes for AWS Config rules.").
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Proactive rules are now taught in the Config subsection, right after the trigger table (config-guide-proactive-vs-detective).

findings.quote: Security Hub CSPM [also receives findings from other AWS services] ... | Every finding in one list | Security Hub | ... **Decision.** Managed services in all accounts, with findings in Security Hub.
findings.evidence: Rule: RULINGS hard rule 8 (one term per concept). The chapter switches between "Security Hub", "AWS Security Hub" and "Security Hub CSPM" for the same job. In this subsection the heading and table say "Security Hub", steps 2 to 4 describe CSPM facts, and the Go deeper block explains the split only after the steps. The ladder diagram, the signals table and the decision record say "AWS Security Hub", while the Choose table says "Security Hub CSPM". Since 2025-12-02 these are two services (fact security-hub-renamed-cspm), so the reader cannot tell which one an answer option means. Fix: give one rule near the top of the chapter (for example "Security Hub" means the unified service, and "Security Hub CSPM" the checks, the aggregation and the EventBridge feed) and apply it in every table, heading and caption.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: 1-fast.md now expands CSPM and says Security Hub CSPM is the original Security Hub, renamed; the real-world box names CSPM. The diagram alt texts and captions (hero, ladder, after) are spec-bound (L702, L703) and keep "AWS Security Hub": a diagrams-stage change.

findings.quote: Security Hub CSPM is the original Security Hub.
findings.evidence: The fast file never expands CSPM. The expansion (cloud security posture management) appears only in a Go deeper block of 2-deep.md and in 2-services.md. The fast file is the only file that some readers open (READER.md: "Put the short version first"). The Changed recently box that explains the split comes three sections later. Rule: STYLE plain-language rule on unexpanded short forms (exemplar README mistake 9: "unexpanded short forms"). Fix: "Security Hub CSPM (cloud security posture management) is the original Security Hub; see Changed recently."
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): "Security Hub CSPM (cloud security posture management) is the original Security Hub, renamed."

findings.quote: | Whose compliance? | Yours, against [Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)](../facts/security-hub.md#security-hub-cspm-supported-standards) |
findings.evidence: A reader who only skims the table learns "Security Hub CSPM = PCI DSS". Fact security-hub-cspm-supported-standards lists more standards: "the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP) standard developed by AWS, and external compliance frameworks such as the Center for Internet Security (CIS), the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS), and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)". Question 10 then depends on FSBP, which the chapter never names. Fix: "Yours, against standards such as AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP) and PCI DSS".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Cell now: "Yours, against standards such as [AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP)]".

findings.quote: | Agent or log setup first? | No: it [pulls independent data streams directly] | [using the Amazon EC2 Systems Manager (SSM) agent](../facts/inspector.md#inspector-ec2-agent-or-agentless), or agentless | No agent |
findings.evidence: Two problems. (1) The row asks a yes/no question, and the Inspector cell gives no yes/no answer. It also leaves out that only EC2 scanning involves an agent. (2) "Amazon EC2 Systems Manager" is a former name (now AWS Systems Manager). RULINGS hard rule 6 says "Current AWS names only", and a former name may appear once, as "formerly". The same display appears twice more in 2-deep.md line 86. Fix: "On EC2: the SSM Agent or agentless scans; no agent for ECR or Lambda", and file a display request for a shorter, current-name display of fact inspector-ec2-agent-or-agentless.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Inspector cell now: "No. Without the Systems Manager (SSM) Agent, it [collects software inventory using Amazon EBS snapshots]". The former-name display is gone from 1-fast.md and from 2-deep.md step 1 (now [AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent)]).

findings.quote: ## In one breath (2 min)
findings.evidence: Lint W201: "`In one breath` has 238 words; the section allows 0 to 200". The overflow comes from the six-step figure list and the startup box. READER.md: "Long LLM-generated text intimidates her". Fix: cut the numbered list under the figure to the caption plus three short lines, or move steps 5 and 6 to the caption.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): The startup example was cut (238 to 224 words). The rest of the section is the one-breath definition, the required problem field and the hero alt text and steps, which must equal the spec (L702, L703). W201 is a warning.

findings.quote: ### GuardDuty analyzes its own copy of your logs and stores none of them (4 min)
findings.evidence: Exemplar README item 3: "Every heading is a true claim on its own". "Its own copy of your logs" suggests that your logs must exist before GuardDuty can copy them, which is the belief of trap detection-trap-guardduty-needs-log-setup. Fact guardduty-faq-no-need-to-enable-source-logs says that GuardDuty "pulls independent data streams directly". Fix: "GuardDuty reads its own streams of your activity and keeps none of the logs".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): The H3 text is fixed by brief.json (L905), and question and task sections link its anchor. The table and exam signal teach that GuardDuty pulls its own streams.

findings.quote: | DNS logs | No, with the AWS DNS resolvers | No |
findings.evidence: The cell is a compressed condition that a second-language reader cannot easily expand: it means "No, if your instances use the AWS DNS resolvers". The table also gives away the answer to the Stop and answer below it, so the question no longer tests what the skim misses (READER.md). Fix: "No, but only when instances use the AWS DNS resolvers". Then make the Stop and answer change a different variable, or leave the condition out of the table and keep it in the step text.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): DNS cell: "No, if instances use the AWS DNS resolvers". The Stop and answer now changes another variable: DNS query logging is off; does GuardDuty still get DNS data? (Yes; the resolver is the condition.)

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A new CVE is published for a package on an EC2 instance that has not changed for a month. Does the team have to start a scan?
findings.evidence: The heading ("Inspector rescans a workload when a new vulnerability is published") and the table row ("EC2 instance | A changed package or a new CVE") answer the question word for word. Exemplar README item 7: "The Stop and answer changes one variable and cannot be copied." Fix: change one variable that the skim does not give. Example: the instance has no SSM Agent; can Inspector still scan it, and from what? (Answer: agentless scanning from EBS snapshots, fact inspector-ec2-agent-or-agentless.) This also ties to the vague Say it line "how it reaches each instance".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Stop and answer now: instance A has the SSM Agent and instance B has none; which finding can come later? (B: agentless scans run [every 24 hours].)

findings.quote: 4. **Keep.** Export findings before the service deletes them. ... | GuardDuty findings | [90 days] | ... | Config configuration items | [7 years (2557 days)] by default |
findings.evidence: This subsection mixes two ideas: AWS Artifact, and how long GuardDuty, Macie and Config keep evidence. The retention table and the Stop and answer about GuardDuty findings sit under an Artifact heading, so a reader who skims headings never finds the retention rule. Question 8 (GuardDuty finding retention) links its Review to this Artifact section. Exemplar README item 1: one subsection runs one problem through trace, table and reason. Fix: give retention its own short subsection with an assertion heading (for example "Findings expire inside each service, so long retention needs an export to S3"), or move the table to the GuardDuty subsection, and point Question 8's Review there.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): A new subsection is not in brief.json (L905, L106; orchestrator). The retention table that duplicated the A-list was removed from the Artifact subsection; the A-list holds the numbers, and q010 is no longer shipped.

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** An auditor wants a year of GuardDuty findings that were never exported. What can the team give, and what should it change?
findings.evidence: The retention table just above it ("GuardDuty findings | 90 days") and step 4 ("Export findings before the service deletes them") give the answer. Exemplar README item 7. Fix: ask about Security Hub CSPM, which keeps a finding 90 days after its last update (fact security-hub-finding-retention-90-days). The reader then has to apply the rule to a service that the table does not list.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Stop and answer now asks about Security Hub CSPM findings ([90 days] after the last update; copy them out through EventBridge).

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A company must know when an **access key** calls APIs from an unusual geolocation. Which service, and which evidence?
findings.evidence: The bold step label "**Activity.** Amazon GuardDuty reads API calls" and the ladder caption answer both parts from a skim. Exemplar README item 7. The question practices recall of the map, not reasoning. Fix: use a stem whose evidence words mislead, for example an unusual API call that changes a security group, where the reader must separate GuardDuty (who called, malicious activity) from Config (what the group looks like now).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Stop and answer now: an access key opens a security group to the internet; which service flags the call (GuardDuty) and which shows the old rules (Config)?

findings.quote: 5. **Investigate.** You pivot [directly into the Detective console](../facts/detective.md#detective-pivot-from-guardduty-security-hub).
findings.evidence: Detective is taught in one step, one table row and one Stop and answer. The deep file never explains "behavior graph", but Question 1 (the worked example) keys on "review the activity of the role in the behavior graph", and Question 9 uses it in a distractor. "Pivot" (jargon) and "Triage" (in the Why line) are not explained for a second-language reader (STYLE plain English; RULINGS hard rule 8). The reader could not explain Detective to a customer from this text. Fix: one step that says what Detective builds (a behavior graph from CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow Logs and GuardDuty findings, fact detective-core-sources), and replace "pivot" with "open the finding in Detective from the GuardDuty or Security Hub console".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Step 5 now defines the behavior graph, [a linked set of extracted and analyzed data] (detective-behavior-graph-definition); "pivot" and "Triage" are gone from 2-deep.md.

findings.quote: | An automatic response | An EventBridge rule |
findings.evidence: Detecting a finding and responding to it automatically (finding to an EventBridge rule to a Lambda function or Systems Manager Automation that isolates an instance or blocks an IP address) is a frequent exam pattern for task 1.2/1.3. In this chapter it is one table row with no trace, no Exam signal and no question. Facts already in the canon would carry it: guardduty-findings-console-and-eventbridge, security-hub-cspm-eventbridge-all-findings, macie-findings-auto-to-eventbridge, guardduty-eventbridge-subsequent-occurrences-default-6-hours. Fix: a short Go deeper block or a 4-step trace (finding, EventBridge rule, target, action), with an Exam signal for "automatically respond to GuardDuty findings".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: the table row now reads "An EventBridge rule and a Lambda function". A Go deeper trace with guardduty-automated-remediation-eventbridge-lambda was written and removed because the deep file is at its 2,400-word limit (L201) and at most 3 Go deeper blocks (L106).

findings.quote: 2. **Pull.** It reads CloudTrail management events, VPC flow logs and [DNS logs](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-foundational-sources-list) as its own streams.
findings.evidence: The GuardDuty subsection teaches only the foundational sources. The fast traps, the services card and Questions 3, 7 and 9 rely on "GuardDuty S3 Protection" and "GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3", which the deep file names only in one sentence of the Macie subsection. The reader cannot reason about which GuardDuty feature to turn on for S3 threats or for malware in uploads. Fix: a two-row table or a Go deeper block, "foundational sources (always on) and protection plans that you turn on (S3 Protection: S3 data events; Malware Protection for S3: new uploads)", using facts guardduty-s3-protection-data-events and guardduty-malware-s3-scans-new-uploads-managed.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): A protection-plans Go deeper was written and removed because the deep file is at its 2,400-word limit (L201) and at most 3 Go deeper blocks (L106). The fast table now says "for its foundational sources", the fast trap names GuardDuty S3 Protection, and the Macie subsection names Malware Protection for S3.

findings.quote: **Spot the bug.** A team aggregates findings in us-east-1 from a linked us-west-2, and enabled Security Hub CSPM and AWS Config in us-east-1 only.
findings.evidence: "Linked" Region and "home Region" are never defined. Step 3 says only "Findings go to a single home Region" and does not say that the other Regions are called linked Regions or that each must have the service enabled. The sentence also mixes tenses ("aggregates ... and enabled"). Rule: STYLE plain English, one term per concept, defined at first use. Fix: in step 3, "You choose one home Region; the other Regions, called linked Regions, send their findings to it", and "has enabled" in the Spot the bug.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Step 3 now: "Linked Regions send their findings [to a single home Region]"; the Spot the bug says "has enabled".

findings.quote: Why does AWS work this way? Triage needs one queue, and Detective has [no additional software to deploy](../facts/detective.md#detective-no-queries-to-build).
findings.evidence: Exemplar README item 4: one Why reason per subsection, "said as a customer would hear it". This line joins two unrelated points and explains neither cause. The first subsection's Why ("detection consists of two parts") also does not explain why AWS splits detection across four services. Fix, for example: "Why two services? Gathering findings and investigating one finding need different data. Security Hub needs every finding in one list. Detective needs months of activity around one finding." (ground the data part in detective-core-sources).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Why now: "The two jobs need different data: Security Hub needs every finding, and Detective needs the activity around one."

findings.quote: > **Say it:** The short answer is: Inspector rescans when a new CVE appears. The thing to watch is how it reaches each instance.
findings.evidence: Exemplar README item 6: the watch move must be something the reader can say to a customer. "How it reaches each instance" is vague: the subsection means SSM Agent or agentless EBS-snapshot scanning but never says so in this line. Fix: "The thing to watch is the SSM Agent: without it, Inspector scans EBS snapshots instead."
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Say it now ends "The thing to watch is the SSM Agent." (the 25-word Say it limit, L202, blocks the longer line).

findings.quote: No. Inspector keeps [automatically rescanning resources in response to changes](...), such as [a new common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE)](...).
findings.evidence: "A new common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE)" is ungrammatical (a plural expansion after "a"), and the CVE expansion is repeated after step 2 already gave it. Fix: "such as a newly published CVE".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): The Stop and answer was rewritten; the ungrammatical display is no longer used in 2-deep.md.

findings.quote: | [6 hours](...) | Default event interval for repeated GuardDuty findings | Faster needs [15 minutes](...) |
findings.evidence: "Faster needs 15 minutes" does not say what the reader does. Fact guardduty-eventbridge-subsequent-occurrences-default-6-hours: "As an administrator account, you can customize the default frequency ... Possible values are 15 minutes, 1 hour, or the default 6 hours." This is an A-list row and card detection-c006, so she will memorize it. Fix: "The administrator account can set 15 minutes or 1 hour".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Same fix as claims-06.

findings.quote: > **The exam probably expects:** no custom rules, only [your own threat lists](...). Do not let this number decide an answer.
findings.evidence: The change is a feature, not a number, so "this number" has nothing to refer to. The exemplar formula fits a quota change, not this case. "Your own threat lists" is also never explained (fact guardduty-faq-no-custom-detections: "adding your own threat lists and trusted IP address list"). Fix: "Do not let this feature decide an answer.", and spell out "your own lists of known bad IP addresses (threat lists) and trusted IP addresses".
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: "only [your own threat lists] of known bad IP addresses". The ending "Do not let this number decide an answer." is the fixed form of STYLE 11.11.

findings.quote: > **Say it:** The short answer is: Macie finds sensitive data in S3 and flags public buckets. The thing to watch is that Macie reads text.
findings.evidence: This Say it line comes right before the Stop and answer about audio in callvale-audio and gives its answer away. "Macie reads text" is also looser than the source, which names the formats that Macie skips: "Macie doesn't analyze data in images, or audio, video, and other types of multimedia content." (fact macie-no-images-audio-video). Fix: make the watch move "The thing to watch is the file type: Macie skips images, audio and video." and let the Stop and answer apply it to a new case (for example scanned PDFs of complaint letters as images).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Say it now: "The thing to watch is the file type." The Stop and answer still has to apply it to audio.

findings.quote: 2. **Sample and match.** Automated discovery samples objects.
findings.evidence: "Automated discovery" and "managed data identifiers" are new terms used in the trace without a plain meaning. The contrast with a discovery job comes three paragraphs later, in the Why line. Questions 3 and 9 key on "sensitive data discovery job" and "managed data identifiers". Fix: bold both at first use and add a short gloss ("automated discovery: Macie checks a sample of your objects every day", "managed data identifiers: built-in patterns for data such as card numbers").
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: "Managed data identifiers (built-in patterns)". Automated discovery is glossed by the sampling Why line below the trace.

findings.quote: 1. **Delegate.** A security account [serves as the administrator account](...).
findings.evidence: "Delegated administrator" appears in Questions 2, 6, 8 and 9 and in the decision record figure, but this chapter never says what it means or that it is set up through AWS Organizations, and there is no cross-reference. Fix: add a short gloss or an xref marker to the Organizations chapter ("a member account that the management account allows to manage the service for the whole organization").
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): xref marker to chapter 04 (delegated administrator) on the Delegate step.

findings.quote: Nothing here yet.
findings.evidence: TOOLS-items.md: "Only items with `status: ready` are printed". findings.quote: Open the finding in AWS Security Hub CSPM, and create an insight that groups the related findings of the role. ... Create a GuardDuty suppression rule for the finding type
findings.evidence: The worked example, the one question with a full think-aloud, rejects options on three terms that the chapter never teaches: "insight", "suppression rule" and "behavior graph". The Why not lines explain suppression rules (fact guardduty-suppression-rule-still-generates), but "insight" and "behavior graph" are never explained anywhere. A reader who studied the chapter cannot follow step 4 of the think-aloud. findings.quote: The delegated administrator exports for the organization, so one setting covers every member account.
findings.evidence: RULINGS hard rule 1, and exemplar README mistake 2 ("An order or mechanism that no fact gives"). This sentence carries the key of Question 8 against the per-account Lambda option, and it has no fact link. The linked fact guardduty-export-findings-to-s3 only says you can "optionally export the generated findings" to S3. It does not say that the administrator's export covers member findings, and it does not cover the cross-account bucket in the log archive account. Fix: ground it with a fact from the GuardDuty export page (administrator account and member findings), or reword the key so it does not depend on that claim.

findings.quote:

- **Managed detection services for the organization.**
findings.evidence: The two rejected options get no reason, and the hidden comment shows that the before picture is still missing. The reader sees the decision but not why the other options lose (operational effort, the 90-day evidence gap, no single place for findings). The exemplar decision record gives a reason per option. findings.quote: | "a single view of security findings" | AWS Security Hub | it [also receives findings from other AWS services](...) |
findings.evidence: "also" comes from the source sentence and has no referent in the table cell, so a skimming reader asks "also, besides what?". Fix: "it receives findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and other services", keeping the fact link on a display without "also" if one exists.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): "beside its checks" was tried and removed for the 1,000-word fast limit. The link text must hold a display of the fact (L303), and the display contains "also".
